newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-GIANTS SIGN BONDS TO TWO-YEAR, TOP-PAY CONTRACT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GIANTS SIGN BONDS TO TWO-YEAR, TOP-PAY CONTRACT.

text.p: The San Francisco Giants and three-time National League Most Valuable Player Barry Bonds have agreed to a two-year contract extension that again will make him baseball's highest-paid player.

The deal, announced Thursday night, includes a club option for 2001, but is worth $22.9 million over two years if the team exercises a $2.5 million buyout clause in the option year, said Dennis Gilbert, Bonds' agent.
The $11.45 million average salary surpasses the $11 million that Chicago White Sox slugger Albert Belle will be paid annually over the next five years.

Bonds last year became just the second player in baseball history to collect 40 home runs and 40 stolen bases in the same season. The first was Jose Canseco, who performed the feat in 1988 for the Oakland Athletics.
The 32-year-old Bonds finished fifth in balloting for National League MVP in 1996 after hitting .308 with 42 homers, a career-high 129 RBI, 40 stolen bases and a National League-record 151 walks.
